effect.words: Whose names did the water take?
effect.reply: My grandmother was Mirebridge-born. Every Restday she said them over the pans: the ferry wolf, the trapper by the causeway, the pup who rang the bell. Carry them to whoever keeps the Book of Names. Somebody ought to.

quests.title: The Badger Under the Apple Store
quests.summary: A badger has dug in under the Plumtree apple store. Bring it down for the orchard keeper.

offer.say: #greet#. A badger's dug in under my apple store and leaves me short-weighed every night. It'll run, mind, but corner it and it bites. Follow your nose from the hedges. Bring it down and I'll pay full weight. Scales and silver, I'd go myself, but not into that wood.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Full weight, as promised, and dried apples on top. You'll not get a bargain like that in the city, eh? My grandmother would've seen it off with a broom. Yours, I couldn't say.

objectives.label: Bring down the badger by the Plumtree apple store.

quests.title: Swill for Southwood
quests.summary: Carry meal and oats from Larkfield Stores out to the Southwood pig yard.

offer.say: #greet#. Southwood's pigs eat more than the whole of Larkfield, and the granary's short-weighing us this month. Two of meal and two of oats from the stores, carried out to the yard, eh? I keep a tally. You'll be on the good side of it.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. That's one in the tally, #address#, and I don't forget a mark. I owe a wolf in Ridgemere more than I'll say, so it's good to have something owed the other way. Good trading.

objectives.label: Bring the swineherd two of meal from Larkfield Stores.
Bring the swineherd two of oats.

quests.title: Old Linen for the Paper Vats
quests.summary: The Larkfield Print House makes its paper from old linen, and the vats are low.

offer.say: #greet#. Old linen, beaten to pulp. Good paper's made from linen, and the vats are low. Two lengths of linen cloth will do; the stores keep a bolt or two. I've carted to Ridgemere for it once this week, and I'll not do it twice. The press pays full weight.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Into the vat it goes. Every sheet the press runs starts as somebody's old shirt, eh? Take a couple of sheets yourself; you'll find a use for them. Fair price to you.

objectives.label: Bring the vat hand two lengths of linen cloth.

quests.title: Reeds in the Mill Race
quests.summary: The Longmead mill race is choking on reeds. Pull four bundles from the bank and bring them to the miller.

offer.say: #greet#. The mill race is choking on reeds again and the wheel's turning light. Pull four bundles from the bank by the mill and bring them here, eh? I'd do it myself, but I start humming and forget why I'm standing in the water.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Hear that? Full weight on the wheel again. Take some flour, ground fine and top-weight. I'll hum you a march for the road, and you'll not get it out of your head till Restday.

objectives.label: Pull four bundles of reeds from the bank by Longmead Mill.

quests.title: Smoke for the Hives
quests.summary: Bees go gentle in smoke. Bring herbs for the Larkholm smoker, and mind the camp up the Sunfields road.

offer.say: #greet#. Larkholm keeps a row of skeps by the granary wall, and I mind them. Bees go gentle in smoke, and my smoker's empty. Three bunches of herbs to burn; wormwood's best, if the season's given any. And mind the Sunfields road. There's wolves camped up there who aren't after honey.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Here's honey off the Larkholm skeps, ripe as it gets. I walked to Ridgemere once and back on a comb like this. Mind the bees on your way out; they don't know you yet.

objectives.label: Bring the Larkholm farmhand three bunches of herbs for his smoker.
Wormwood burns best: bring two bunches, if the summer or autumn grass has any.
Bring down a bandit of the camp up the Sunfields road.

quests.title: The Miller's Wager
quests.summary: Hares are eating Larkholm's young wheat. One hare earns pay; two win the miller's wager.

offer.say: #greet#. Hares in my seed rows, eating the young wheat to stubble. One hare, and I'll pay. Two, and you've won a wager: two of flour says you can't. They go like a windfall rolling downhill.
offer.decline: I'll not take your bet today.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Sheaf and sickle, that's a hare fewer in my rows. If it's my flour you've won, don't tell the granary; they think I'm careful. I know a tale about a great House that'd curl your ears, but a wager's one thing and a tale's another.

objectives.label: Bring down a hare in the Larkholm fields.
Take a second hare there and win the miller's wager.

quests.title: Garlands for the Square
quests.summary: Southmeadow dresses its square for the festival, and every wolf's green goes on one rope.

offer.say: #greet#. The festival's on us and the square's as bare as a stubble field. Bring me green things for the garlands: herbs, and any flowers the season's left. Every wolf's bunch goes on one rope. When it reaches round the square, Southmeadow's ready.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Ripe, that, and on the rope already. My mother strung this rope, and hers before her, and I feel the both of them watching. I'd not have taken green from a stranger's paw once. I'll take yours.

objectives.label: Bring the Larkholm farmhand two bunches of herbs for the garland rope.
Any flowers the season has left: lavender, chamomile or rose petals.
Enter a contest at the Southmeadow festival, on festival day.

quests.title: Twine for the Purse-Nets
quests.summary: The Dune warrener's purse-nets are worn through. Bring him cord to knit new ones.

offer.ask: What are those little nets for?
offer.say: #greet#. Purse-nets, for the burrow mouths. A rabbit bolts into one and it draws shut. Mine are worn through, and a worn net is a rabbit's best friend, as my father said. Two lengths of cord and I'll knit new ones. Straw for the hutches too, if you've any.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. A mended net catches what a new one only promises, they say. Take a smoked one for the road. And mind the soft ground by the burrows; it's riddled.

objectives.label: Bring the warrener two lengths of cord.
Straw for the hutches, if you have it.

quests.title: Fire Under the Pans
quests.summary: The Fenside salt pans boil on firewood, and the fen has none worth burning.

offer.say: #greet#. The pans boil on firewood, and the fen's got none worth burning. Four armfuls from the dry ground and the salt comes up white. Peat too, if you've the back for it. My grandmother carried peat on her head and called it a hat.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. White as a wedding cloth, that'll come up. Take a measure of salt. If you see lights out on the fen, don't follow them. My grandmother said they were only the marsh. She said a lot of things.

objectives.label: Bring the salt worker four armfuls of firewood from the dry ground.
Peat, if you have the back for it.

quests.title: Grey Clay from the Mirebridge Pits
quests.summary: The Fenshore Kilns want more clay than one digger can dig. Dig four lumps at the Mirebridge pits.

offer.ask: Is that all yours to dig?
offer.say: #greet#. The kilns want twice the clay the old potter did, and I'm one wolf with one spade. Dig me four lumps here at the pits, and I'll cart them in with mine. Four. I'll count them. Don't stand long at the old crossroads on the way. That's where the village was.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Four, and good grey ones. I counted. Most wolves bring three and call it four. Take a pot from the kilns' last firing; it leans, but it holds.

objectives.label: Dig four lumps of clay at the Mirebridge pits.
Give the four lumps to the clay digger.
Stand a moment at the Mirebridge crossroads, where the village was.

quests.title: A Plank Gone by the Heron
quests.summary: A plank has gone on the Fenshore boardwalk by the Heron. Bring planks and nails for the deckhand who mends it.

offer.ask: Is that a gap in the boardwalk?
offer.say: #greet#. There's a plank gone on the boardwalk by the Heron, and the next wolf through will be wet to the knee, no? Two planks and a paw of nails, and I'll do the hammering. I don't hurry, mind, but what I mend stays mended.
offer.handIn: Planks and nails for the boardwalk.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Dry feet for the next one through, fen-sure, and that's the best thanks the fen gives. I know a tale about a great House that'd sink a boardwalk, but I'll keep it. Some planks hold better nailed down.

objectives.label: Bring the deckhand two planks.
Bring her a paw of nails: four will do.
If you carry the Shortcut Gift, blink across the gap before it is mended.

quests.title: Salt for the Stores
quests.summary: Carry two measures of the Saltpan's salt across the white to the Saltwell storekeeper.

offer.ask: Is the Saltwell store out of salt?
offer.say: #greet#. The salt is raked at the pan, but the stores are empty, and no carter will go into the white while the sun is high. Without salt I cannot cure a single pelt. Carry these two measures to the storekeeper for me. A favour carried is a favour owed, and I keep count.
offer.handIn: Your salt is at the stores.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. You walked it in the heat and did not complain. My mother kept this warren, and hers before her, and none of them had a wolf like you to call on. That is one in my tally, #address#. The well remembers who drew from it.

objectives.label: Carry the two measures of salt to the Saltwell storekeeper.
If you carry the Lighten Load Gift, use it on the road.

quests.title: Rabbits in the Vines
quests.summary: Rabbits strip the young vines at Ochre to the stalk. Bring down two in the vineyard.

offer.say: #greet#. The rabbits come in from the scrub and strip my young vines to the stalk. Bring down two of them, and the rest will learn. Do this, and you are welcome at my table, by bread and salt.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Sit, take grapes; they are sweet this year. A stranger who hunts like a wolf of the wadi. I did not think I would see it. Perhaps not everything that comes up the road is brackish.

objectives.label: Bring down two rabbits in the Ochre vines.

quests.title: Water and a Word
quests.summary: When a cart or a wagon comes in off the sand, someone must meet it at the Saltwell well, then break bread at the Oasis Inn.

offer.ask: Who meets the wagons when they come in?
offer.say: #greet#. When a cart or a wagon comes in off the sand, someone must meet it at the well with water and a word. The innkeeper cannot leave the fire. The farm cart comes in early, most mornings. Be at the well when it does, then come inside and break bread. That is how Saltwell says welcome.
offer.handIn: They were met, and I broke bread inside.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. They will tell it on the road: at Saltwell, someone met us. Every wagon comes home at last, and this one came home to you. I dream of a farm, you know, somewhere green. But I would miss this.

objectives.label: Be at the well on the Saltwell square when a cart or a wagon comes in (the farm cart comes early, most mornings).
Break bread at the Oasis Inn: buy a bowl or a cup there, or eat beside someone who is eating.
If you carry the Dowse Gift, find where the old wells of Saltwell ran.
